title: Tenant window stitching and lease-offset reconciliation for reserved capacity quotas
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Production incidents revealed inconsistent reserved-capacity quota windows when tenants switch timezones, have overlapping lease handoffs, or during controller failovers. This ticket defines a deterministic approach to stitch tenant rolling windows, reconcile lease offsets, and produce an auditable correction ledger to ensure accounting correctness across daily/monthly resets and rolling windows for reserved pools.
problem_statement: Observed behaviors: (1) Tenants who change timezone or have non-UTC epoch anchors see shifted quota epochs leading to transient overages. (2) During reserved pool failover we observe double-counted burst allowances for a small subset of requests due to lease overlap. (3) Backfilled usage from ingestion pipelines occasionally applies to the wrong epoch boundary because of inconsistent watermarking. These cause billing disputes and SLA violations for Dedicated customers.
proposal_summary: Introduce a tenant-level epoch stitching service that atomicizes lease handoffs and records offset deltas into a correction ledger. Use deterministic epoch anchors (UTC-based with tenant-configurable alignment window), idempotent lease tokens, and a periodic reconciler that emits correction events applied to the billing ledger with audit metadata.
acceptance_criteria: 1) No tenant experiences >1% unexplained quota drift across epoch boundaries in the canary group (2 tenants) over a 7-day window.
2) Lease handoff protocol prevents overlapping effective allocation windows: all handoffs are either seamless or compensated via correction ledger within 5 minutes.
3) All reconciliation adjustments are auditable: reconciler emits correction events with original and corrected epoch, reason code, and idempotency token.
4) Billing pipeline applies correction events without modifying original raw usage records (corrections are additive and reversible).
5) Integration tests for timezone changes, controller failover, and backfill ingestion pass in CI.
6) Dashboard panels for correction volume, reconciler latency, and correction success rate are added and green (SLO >99.5% success).
implementation_notes: Design a compact epoch identifier: YYYYMMDD:anchor-offset where anchor is UTC midnight and offset is tenant-configured window-shift in minutes.
Lease token semantics: create, renew, release. Tokens carry start_ts, end_ts, and an idempotency key. Handoffs require previous token release acknowledgement or reconciler-generated compensation.
Correction ledger format: correction_id, tenant_id, original_epoch, corrected_epoch, delta_units, reason_code, reconciler_run_id, created_at, applied=false/true.
Reconciler job: streaming consumer over lease events + usage stream, runs incremental reconciliation every 1 minute and full reconciles nightly for 30 days of history.
Safety: reconciler must cap any single correction to a configurable percentage of tenant quota to avoid large billing surprises; large changes require manual review flag.
Backfill handling: backfilled records must include source_ingest_ts and target_epoch_hint; reconciler validates and assigns to epoch or issues correction events.
Idempotency: all correction events must be idempotent via correction_id and reconciler_run_id to allow retries after controller crashes.
Operational hooks: expose a dry-run mode, a manual-apply workflow for outlier corrections, and an emergency rollback path that marks corrections as reversed.
Migration: a three-step rollout (canary tenants -> staged cohort -> global) with nightly dry-run comparisons against current billing to measure delta before flip.
DB schema: append-only correction_ledger table partitioned by tenant and month; ensure TTL for older audit rows per compliance policy (retain 2 years).

rollout_plan: Step 0 (Dry run): Enable reconciler in dry-run mode for all tenants for 7 days and capture correction deltas without applying.
Step 1 (Canary): Apply corrections for 2 low-risk Dedicated tenants for 72 hours, monitor correction volume and customer alerts.
Step 2 (Staged): Expand to 10% of Dedicated tenants over 2 weeks with nightly audits and manual review for large adjustments.
Step 3 (Full): Flip global apply-on for reserved pools with continuous monitoring and an automated rollback trigger on correction error rate >0.5%.
Communications: notify affected customers 48 hours before Step 2 and provide a correction history export per tenant.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Large retroactive corrections upsetting customers. Mitigation: cap automatic corrections and surface manual review for >threshold deltas.
Risk: Reconciler introduces load on billing pipeline. Mitigation: rate-limit correction apply path and use backpressure signals to pause reconciler.
Risk: Timezone/anchor misconfiguration. Mitigation: default to UTC anchor and provide safe migration script with dry-run outputs.
Risk: Data retention/compliance conflict. Mitigation: consult security/compliance and implement retention policy in DB schema.
